raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
When expert-parallel ranks receive unequal token counts, legacy token-dropping gates can allocate different dispatch capacities before equal-split all-to-all. Dropless top-1 can also shrink the already-agreed capacity back to its local token count. This can hang both training forward and backward.

Fixes https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/issues/6809.

## Change

- Agree the final capacity with MAX inside the explicit EP group for top-1, top-2, and top-k, in both token-drop modes. Dropping uses the maximum configured capacity; dropless dispatch uses the maximum expert occupancy.
- Keep communication capacity separate from the existing bounded local top-k row selection. Remove the dropless top-1 local capacity clamp.
- Round capacity to the non-expert TP size because the dispatcher splits this dimension before expert execution. None/singleton EP groups continue to avoid collectives.

Routing-weight normalization, auxiliary-loss formulas, public signatures, and checkpoint/config formats are unchanged. Smaller input ranks can retain more tokens and send additional padding. Token-dropping EP adds one scalar MAX collective per MoE forward; the dropless branch still performs one MAX.

## Validation

Hardware: same-node **2 x RTX 4090 24GB**, driver **580.76.05**, torch **2.12.1+cu130**, CUDA **13.0**, NCCL **2.29.7**, Python **3.12.3**. Base: **f818504999bdd57c3e771368aefc301290020d9a**.

Before the fix, with 128/257 tokens, four experts, hidden=32, k=1, capacity_factor=1, drop_tokens=True, the actual all-to-all inputs are `(4,32,32)` / `(4,65,32)`. The training reproducer hangs and exits 124 under a 50-second timeout. After the fix, both ranks send `(4,65,32)` and complete forward, backward, and SGD update.

Before/after regression evidence:

- Capacity-contract tests: baseline **10 failed / 6 passed**; fixed **16 passed**. Covers dense/sparse outputs, both token-drop modes, k=1/2/4, and probability/position top-k selection.
- Training reference: **24 passed**. EP=2 outputs, auxiliary loss, input/gate/expert gradients, and SGD-updated parameters match a full EP=1 model using the same agreed capacity, for 128/257 and 129/129 tokens in FP32/BF16.
- TP split/gather forward and backward: baseline **8 failed / 4 passed**; fixed **12 passed**, combining the expert-TP enabled and disabled runs at EP=1, TP=2, three tokens. The failures pin odd capacity and the top-1 local clamp.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=tests DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT=60 pytest --forked \
  tests/unit/v1/moe/test_moe.py::TestMoEUnevenTokens \
  tests/unit/v1/moe/test_moe_tp.py::TestMoECapacityTensorParallel
```

Additional DeepSpeed engine validation uses the two-layer `SimpleMoEModel` (hidden=32, four experts, SGD, ZeRO-0, no offload). It covers 24 equal-token and 24 uneven-token combinations of FP32/BF16, both drop modes, k=1/2/4, and gradient accumulation=1/4, with eight optimizer updates per combination. All updates and losses remain finite. Equal-token losses match the baseline exactly; maximum parameter differences are 1.49e-8 (FP32) and 9.77e-4 (BF16), within precision-specific tolerances. An unmodified-baseline repeat itself differs by 1.49e-8 in FP32, so no bitwise-state equivalence is claimed.

Existing MoE regression: **34 passed, 28 skipped** (four-rank cases and unavailable Tutel), including FP16 SimpleMoE at ZeRO 0/1/2, FP32 expert-gradient comparison at ZeRO 0/1/2, dense/sparse dispatch and tracing capacity tests. Changed-file pre-commit passes.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=tests DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT=120 pytest --forked \
  tests/unit/v1/moe/test_moe.py tests/unit/v1/moe/test_moe_tp.py \
  -k "not TestMoEUnevenTokens and not TestMoECapacityTensorParallel and not TestMoEFP16GradientNorm"
```

A separate two-layer **legacy MoE + SGD training microbenchmark** uses hidden=1024, FFN=4096, 16 experts, EP=2, TP=1, drop_tokens=True; 129/129 or 128/257 tokens, three warmup updates and 16 measured updates. Times are wall-clock, synchronized, using the slowest rank per step; memory is maximum PyTorch allocated memory per GPU during measured steps. This is a single run per configuration. Equal-input loss traces match baseline. The added agreement has a measured latency cost (equal-input median approximately 35–40 ms after the fix versus 31–37 ms before); it does not change equal-input peak allocated memory.

| Precision / k | Equal baseline tokens/s | Equal fixed tokens/s | Equal peak MiB | Uneven fixed tokens/s | Uneven peak MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| float32 / 1 | 8047 | 7134 | 1042.45 | 11262 | 1043.79 |
| float32 / 2 | 7327 | 6615 | 1042.77 | 9719 | 1044.45 |
| float32 / 4 | 7895 | 7010 | 1044.06 | 10383 | 1046.40 |
| bfloat16 / 1 | 8303 | 7342 | 529.87 | 11202 | 531.05 |
| bfloat16 / 2 | 7061 | 6453 | 530.03 | 9698 | 531.37 |
| bfloat16 / 4 | 7832 | 7101 | 530.35 | 10128 | 532.01 |

The uneven-input baseline cannot complete communication, so no throughput baseline is reported for it. These are short correctness/overhead measurements with SGD, not full-model quality convergence or Adam memory measurements.

## Scope and overlap

Duplicate checks included #6809 in PR bodies and capacity/agreement/uneven/all-to-all keywords. No same-scope implementation was found. Merged #8155 bounds local top-k selection; it does not establish EP capacity agreement. #8769 changes optional route normalization; this patch leaves those formulas untouched.

The dense gate and sparse legacy MOELayer paths share this fix. Legacy inference-v1 imports TopKGate; AutoEP and inference-v2 use separate dispatch implementations and are unchanged. Tutel consumes the agreed capacity but was not installed for device testing.

EP=4, simultaneous EP=2 + TP=2, non-CUDA accelerators, Tutel, and full-model quality convergence are not validated here. The available machine has two GPUs; four-rank combinations need additional hardware.

AI assistance was used for implementation, test construction, device execution, and these notes. The human operator explicitly authorized submission and DCO sign-off using their configured Git identity.

+class TestMoEUnevenTokens(DistributedTest):
+    world_size = 2
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("k, drop_policy", [(1, "probs"), (2, "probs"), (4, "probs"), (4, "position")])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("drop_tokens", [True, False])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("sparse_routes", [True, False])
+    def test_capacity_agreement(self, k, drop_policy, drop_tokens, sparse_routes):
+        device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+        num_tokens = (128, 257)[dist.get_rank()]
+        logits = torch.arange(4, device=device, dtype=torch.float32).expand(num_tokens, -1).contiguous()
+        kwargs = dict(drop_tokens=drop_tokens, ep_group=dist.get_world_group(), sparse_routes=sparse_routes)
+        if k == 1:
+            result = top1gating(logits, 1.0, 0, use_rts=False, **kwargs)
+        elif k == 2:
+            result = top2gating(logits, 1.0, 0, top2_2nd_expert_sampling=False, **kwargs)
+        else:
+            result = topkgating(logits, k, 1.0, 0, drop_policy=drop_policy, **kwargs)
+
+        capacity = int(result[1]) if sparse_routes else result[2].shape[-1]
+        # All tokens select the same k experts, so each selected expert needs 257 slots without dropping.
+        expected = (257 * k + 3) // 4 if drop_tokens else 257
+        assert capacity == expected
+        if not sparse_routes and not drop_tokens:
+            assert result[2].sum().item() == num_tokens * k
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("k", [1, 2, 4])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("drop_tokens", [True, False])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("token_counts", [(128, 257), (129, 129)], ids=["uneven", "equal"])
+    def test_training(self, k, drop_tokens, dtype, token_counts):
+        if dtype == torch.bfloat16 and not get_accelerator().is_bf16_supported():
+            pytest.skip("bf16 is not supported on this accelerator")
+
+        rank = dist.get_rank()
+        device = get_accelerator().current_device_name()
+        hidden_dim, num_experts = 8, 4
+        capacity = (max(token_counts) * k + num_experts - 1) // num_experts if drop_tokens else max(token_counts)
+        torch.manual_seed(1234)
+        kwargs = dict(hidden_size=hidden_dim,
+                      expert=torch.nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim, bias=False),
+                      num_experts=num_experts,
+                      k=k,
+                      drop_tokens=drop_tokens,
+                      use_rts=False,
+                      top2_2nd_expert_sampling=False)
+        # EP=1 with this explicit floor independently fixes the communication capacity for the oracle.
+        reference = MoE(ep_size=1, min_capacity=capacity if drop_tokens else 0, **kwargs).to(device=device,
+                                                                                             dtype=dtype)
+        model = MoE(ep_size=self.world_size, min_capacity=0, **kwargs).to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
+        model.set_deepspeed_parallelism()
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            gate_weight = reference.deepspeed_moe.gate.wg.weight
+            gate_weight.zero_()
+            gate_weight[:, 0] = torch.tensor([2, 1, -1, -2], device=device, dtype=dtype)
+            model.deepspeed_moe.gate.load_state_dict(reference.deepspeed_moe.gate.state_dict())
+            reference_experts = reference.deepspeed_moe.experts.deepspeed_experts
+            local_experts = model.deepspeed_moe.experts.deepspeed_experts
+            for index, expert in enumerate(reference_experts):
+                expert.weight.mul_(1 + index * 0.2)
+            for index, expert in enumerate(local_experts):
+                expert.load_state_dict(reference_experts[rank * model.num_local_experts + index].state_dict())
+
+        def check_capacity(module, inputs, output):
+            # Pin the communication-shape contract before all-to-all, so a regression fails without hanging.
+            value = output[1].reshape(1).to(device)
+            capacities = [torch.empty_like(value) for _ in range(self.world_size)]
+            dist.all_gather(capacities, value, group=model.deepspeed_moe.ep_group)
+            assert all(int(value) == capacity for value in capacities)
+
+        model.deepspeed_moe.gate.register_forward_hook(check_capacity)
+        reference_optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(reference.parameters(), lr=0.1)
+        optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
+        reference_inputs, reference_outputs, reference_aux = [], [], []
+        for source_rank, count in enumerate(token_counts):
+            torch.manual_seed(100 + source_rank)
+            inputs = torch.randn(count, hidden_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)
+            # Send top-1/top-2 routes to the other rank's experts, including their backward gradients.
+            inputs[:, 0] = -1 if source_rank == 0 else 1
+            inputs.requires_grad_()
+            output, aux, _ = reference(inputs)
+            (output.float().square().mean() + 0.01 * aux).backward()
+            reference_inputs.append(inputs)
+            reference_outputs.append(output.detach())
+            reference_aux.append(aux.detach())
+
+        inputs = reference_inputs[rank].detach().clone().requires_grad_()
+        output, aux, _ = model(inputs)
+        tolerance = dict(rtol=0.02, atol=0.002) if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else dict(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output, reference_outputs[rank], **tolerance)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(aux, reference_aux[rank], **tolerance)
+        (output.float().square().mean() + 0.01 * aux).backward()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(inputs.grad, reference_inputs[rank].grad, **tolerance)
+        # Raw MoE does not synchronize the replicated gate parameters; sum source-rank losses as in the oracle.
+        gate = model.deepspeed_moe.gate.wg.weight
+        dist.all_reduce(gate.grad, group=model.deepspeed_moe.ep_group)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(gate.grad, reference.deepspeed_moe.gate.wg.weight.grad, **tolerance)
+        for index, expert in enumerate(local_experts):
+            expected = reference_experts[rank * model.num_local_experts + index]
+            torch.testing.assert_close(expert.weight.grad, expected.weight.grad, **tolerance)
+        before_step = [expert.weight.detach().clone() for expert in local_experts]
+        optimizer.step()
+        reference_optimizer.step()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(gate, reference.deepspeed_moe.gate.wg.weight, **tolerance)
+        for index, expert in enumerate(local_experts):
+            expected = reference_experts[rank * model.num_local_experts + index]
+            torch.testing.assert_close(expert.weight, expected.weight, **tolerance)
+        assert any(not torch.equal(before, expert.weight) for before, expert in zip(before_step, local_experts))
+
